name: Tengnoupal
description: District headquarters and hill town at the highest point on the Imphal–Moreh highway (NH-2/AH-1), about 69 km from Imphal. Offers panoramic views of the Manipur valley and surrounding hills; cool climate and fog in monsoon, historically strategic with WWII associations.
facts: HQ of Tengnoupal district (formed 2016 from Chandel)

name: Moreh
description: Major Indo-Myanmar border trade town in Tengnoupal district at the entrance to the Kabaw Valley. Bustling commercial hub with markets, diverse population, and the Indo-Myanmar Friendship Bridge linking to Tamu (Myanmar). Gateway for cross-border trade under India's Act East Policy.
facts: Key point for ASEAN connectivity and trade

name: Yangoupokpi-Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Wildlife sanctuary covering about 185 km² along the Indo-Myanmar border near Moreh. Protects Indo-Burma biodiversity including Hoolock gibbon (India's only ape), bears, serow, and birds like Green Peafowl. Important transboundary corridor; best visited October–April with forest guide.
facts: Home to Hoolock gibbon and other rare species
Flag: some older sources list under Chandel; now primarily Tengnoupal

name: Langol Peak Garden (Tlanglhungbung Leikol)
description: Scenic peak garden in Langol Village, Machi sub-division, about 60 km from Imphal on the Indo-Myanmar road. Linked to Khamba-Thoibi legend (Thoibi-Lei flowers) and WWII Allied camps. Offers panoramic views, picnic spots, thatched huts, and small museum elements; community-developed tourist site.
facts: Associated with Khamba-Thoibi folklore and WWII

name: Kwatha Village
description: Historic Meitei-majority village in the hills of Tengnoupal district, about 16–18 km from Moreh. Unique as the only ancient Meitei settlement in the hill areas; known for bamboo shoot (soibum) cultivation, traditional governance, Lai Haraoba festival, and peaceful coexistence with neighbouring tribal villages. Name derives from betel nut cultivation.
facts: Only Meitei hill village in Manipur
Historic since King Senbi Kiyamba era
